## Conference overview

*Preview by Jonathan Von Tobel, p. 243. Reproduced in full.*


> They say success is the greatest revenge, but in this case of jilted lovers, the Mountain West might have some trouble making the defectors to the new Pac-12 jealous.

> Gone are Boise State, San Diego State, Fresno State, Colorado State and Utah State.

> To replace them, the conference brought in UTEP, Northern Illinois and North Dakota State.

> The Bison have a shot to be the hot new fling, but the Miners and Huskies are projected to be cellar-dwellars in their first seasons in the conference.

> The aforementioned North Dakota State program — which dominated the FCS and the Missouri Valley Football Conference — is one of the short shots to win the Mountain West.

> UNLV and New Mexico are either tied as favorites or have slight variance in their prices to win it all, depending on the shop.

> All three programs have rightful claims to their status as true contenders, but the conference does go slightly deeper than that.

> Hawaii returns quarterback Micah Alejado, who was named preseason Offensive Player of the Year.

> Timmy Chang has improved his win total each season on the island and has both an effective offense and a favorable schedule in conference play.

> There is no doubt the Rainbow Warriors are a dark horse of sorts to win the Mountain West.

> Then there is Troy Calhoun and Air Force.

> The Falcons won nine games over the last two seasons, but Calhoun has an experienced roster, including quarterback Liam Szarka, who led one of the most efficient offenses in the country last season.

> Air Force could absolutely find a way to the table of contenders by season’s end.

> Heartbreak usually leads to change.

> People hit the gym, change their diets and generally try to improve themselves when they get out of a long-term relationship.

> The Mountain West certainly tried to do that with the additions it made, but it’s unlikely those that departed for the Pac-12 are amazed by the changes to the conference.

> Either way, this should be a raucous and volatile season in the Mountain West, and that is great for bettors. mountain west

## Quarterback themes


**From the conference preview (p. 243):**

> Hawaii returns quarterback Micah Alejado, who was named preseason Offensive Player of the Year.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 243*

> The Falcons won nine games over the last two seasons, but Calhoun has an experienced roster, including quarterback Liam Szarka, who led one of the most efficient offenses in the country last season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 243*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 10 of 10 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Air Force Falcons** (p. 244) — An experienced quarterback, returning production from an offense that was one of the most efficient in the country and no expectations.

- **Hawaii Rainbow Warriors** (p. 247) — The injury eventually led to Alejado missing two starts — Sam Houston State and Portland State — but the signal-caller still delivered.

- **Nevada Wolf Pack** (p. 248) — Quarterback is an obvious question for Nevada, but Duncan showed enough in his starts for Hawaii last season that the expectation should be that he wins the job and serves in the role admirably.

- **New Mexico Lobos** (p. 250) — Twelve starters are back from last year’s squad, and among them are quarterback Jack Layne and reigning Defensive Player of the Year Jaxton Eck.

- **North Dakota State Bison** (p. 253) — When Cole Payton was selected by the Eagles with the 178th pick of the NFL Draft, that marked the fifth Bison starting quarterback drafted in the past 11 years.

- **Northern Illinois Huskies** (p. 254) — No returning starters on defense, a new offense and quarterback for the offense and a new conference.

- **San Jose State Spartans** (p. 257) — This season, the offense has a completely new depth chart at quarterback, outside of one-time UCLA transfer Robert McDaniel.

- **UNLV Rebels** (p. 258) — Logic would dictate that UNLV just cannot keep up the run of success at quarterback the program has experienced the last three seasons.

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 243):**

> The Falcons won nine games over the last two seasons, but Calhoun has an experienced roster, including quarterback Liam Szarka, who led one of the most efficient offenses in the country last season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 243*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 10 of 10 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Air Force Falcons** (p. 245) — The Falcons averaged 29.8 points and 407 yards per game last season.

- **Hawaii Rainbow Warriors** (p. 246) — Coming off a nine-win season, one would assume improvement is hard to achieve in 2026, but the ‘Bows have everything they need to get it done.

- **Nevada Wolf Pack** (p. 248) — Quarterback is an obvious question for Nevada, but Duncan showed enough in his starts for Hawaii last season that the expectation should be that he wins the job and serves in the role admirably.

- **New Mexico Lobos** (p. 250) — Head coach Jason Eck and the Lobos took the Mountain West by storm last season with a 9-4 record and six wins in conference play.

- **North Dakota State Bison** (p. 252) — Not many transfers are on this team, and head coach Tim Polasek lost a lot of talent from last year’s team to the transfer portal.

- **Northern Illinois Huskies** (p. 255) — Harley ran this unit last season, so there is some familiarity with the pieces, but this unit is being overhauled in a big way.

- **San Jose State Spartans** (p. 256) — SJSU has not won a bowl game since 2015, and it has not won more than seven games in a single season since 2012 (that lone bowl win was a 6-7 season).

- **UNLV Rebels** (p. 258) — This depth chart seems to have more flaws to it than previous ones, especially with Orji coming off the horrendous injury he suffered last season.
